title: Sikh groups burn Sonia Gandhi's memoir in Delhi
seoTitle: Delhi protest against Sonia Gandhi memoir

tea.why: Protesters object to Sonia Gandhi's account of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots in her new memoir, 'Belonging: A Journey of Love'.
tea.want: The protesters seek justice for the victims of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots.
tea.changed: Nov 12: Members of the Delhi Sikh Gurdwara Management Committee and victims' families burned copies of the memoir at Rakab Ganj Gurdwara.

summary: On November 12, 2026, members of the Delhi Sikh Gurdwara Management Committee (DSGMC) and families of 1984 anti-Sikh riot victims held a protest at the Rakab Ganj Gurdwara in New Delhi. The demonstrators burned copies of Congress leader Sonia Gandhi's recently released memoir, 'Belonging: A Journey of Love'. The protest was led by DSGMC president Harmeet Singh Kalka and general secretary Jagdeep Singh Kahlo. Participants expressed resentment over Gandhi's description of the 1984 violence, arguing that her account failed to accurately reflect historical events and the suffering of the Sikh community. The DSGMC leaders also criticized former prime minister Rajiv Gandhi regarding his past remarks on the riots. The committee stated it would continue its legal efforts to hold those responsible for the violence accountable.
response: No official response reported in the sources.

updates.text: Protesters gathered at the Rakab Ganj Gurdwara to burn copies of Sonia Gandhi's memoir in response to her account of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots.
